..
Issued at 254 PM CDT Sat Aug 1 2026

Ridge of high pressure will remain overhead through tonight
bringing mainly dry conditions, although there could be a few
isolated showers in the north as the warm front moves eastward.
Developing low to are west will bring a breezy southerly flow
through the night as well. Look for mild low temperatures in 
the 60s tonight. Sunday, surface low will move eastward through
the day. Ahead of this low will be breezy to windy southerly
winds, especially in eastern portions of the CWA. HRRR Ensemble
guidance along with forecast soundings showing NBM wind forecast
may be a tough high, thus lowered winds slightly. This brings
winds just below advisory level, although sustained winds could
still approach 30 mph. Of concern with these winds, low
afternoon RH, and an approaching cold front bringing a wind
shift could be some near critical to critical fire weather
conditions. This is especially of concern in southwestern and
some south central portions. There still remains some
uncertainty on how many hours of critical fire weather
conditions are possible given potential timing issues of the
surface front. Thus have held off on any fire highlights. This
southerly flow should bring some increased dewpoints, while the
surface low reinforces the warm air. High temperatures in the
90s to 100s will be found, with perhaps some heat index values
near to over 100 degrees. A heat product may be needed if
confidence remains high these heat index values are reached
before the surface front moves through. This front is also
expected to return wildfire smoke to the surface Sunday
afternoon through Sunday night from west to east. This smoke
could then linger into Monday as northwest winds remain. Lastly
this surface front could still bring showers and thunderstorms,
with an isolated severe weather threat. SPC has maintained the
Marginal Risk for much of central and eastern ND for Sunday,
mainly for Sunday evening through Sunday night. Instability
begins to increase Sunday evening, although capping issues
remain. Some CAMs like the NAMNEST attempt to break this cap
Sunday evening and bring some isolated severe weather potential
within the Marginal Risk. Most CAMs delay thunderstorm
development to the overnight hours when the upper wave moves
through and there are better jet dynamics. Overall the severe
weather threat remains isolated in nature, with large hail and
especially damaging winds being the main threat. Mild
temperatures look to remain for Sunday night with lows in the
mid 50s to mid 60s.

Post frontal day is then in store for Monday. Where the front
continues to push eastward could still see an isolated to
perhaps scattered severe weather threat. SPC has maintained
Marginal to Slight Risks of severe weather in eastern ND as a
result. Mainly large hail and damaging winds will be the main
threats for Monday. Better shear profiles cold bring an isolated
supercell, although higher LCLs should limit the tornado threat.
Otherwise look for a cooler day on Monday with highs near 70 in
the northwest to mid 80s southeast. Breezy to windy northwest
winds will be had for Monday, which continue to bring wildfire
smoke to the surface. Dry conditions behind this front combined
with these gusty winds will bring more widespread near critical
to critical fire weather conditions, especially in the
southwest. If this trend remains then a fire weather highlight
may be needed. Precipitation chances move eastward Monday
evening, and cooler temperatures behind the front are expected
with lows forecast in the 40s west to 50s east. 

Tuesday looks to remain in the cool broad trough pattern. Look
for highs in the 70s as a result with perhaps some breezy winds
at times. Dry conditions could also bring some lower afternoon
RH, especially in the west and south central. Right now the
breezier winds Tuesday do not look to line up with the lowest RH
values, although may be worth monitoring. Warming and mainly dry
trend then remains in the forecast mid to late next week. The
general flow pattern appears to be more northwest, although
there are still some solutions that build the ridge more inland.
This is causing some increased spreads in NBM temperatures
although the overall trend is to return to above normal
temperatures during this time period. Currently the forecast is
mainly dry, although weak waves within this northwest flow could
bring passing shower and thunderstorm chances. Low RH values
could also continue through next week, although currently there
is not a signal for strong wind. With any stronger northwest 
flow this could change and will be worth monitoring.
